sections.title: The first screen plays its entrance as the page appears
sections.summary: When a visitor opens your published funnel, the first screen plays its entrance right away, once. It uses the Screen Entrance you set here; on an older screen that still has Legacy fade-in on (and no Screen Entrance), a simple fade-in; otherwise your theme’s entrance. sections.title: Animation — every setting
sections.summary: How the screen's standard elements (header, image or video, title and subtitle, choices or bullets, paywall products, action bar) animate in when it opens — style, speed, stagger, easing, and per-element overrides, which take priority over the theme's default motion. This guide documents every setting of the Animation block, grouped by area. Each setting matches a real control in the screen editor.

sections.title: Animation section
sections.summary: Screen Entrance sets this screen's entrance style, speed, and stagger. The standard elements then animate in one after another, in a fixed order: header, image or video, title and subtitle, answer choices or feature bullets, paywall products, and action bar, where present. Slides, progress steps, input fields, custom sections, and embedded HTML aren't included. With Screen Entrance off, the screen plays the Legacy fade-in if that toggle is on, otherwise your theme's entrance, if any (shown as 'Inherited from theme'). Advanced adds easing and per-element overrides. Visitors whose device is set to reduce motion see no animation.

sections.title: Where it appears
sections.summary: Covered screen types: HeroContent, Carousel, ListMultiPick, ListSinglePick, GridMultiPick, GridSinglePick, ProgressSteps, TextInput, WheelPicker, HeroList, WebEmbed, Paywall, FlexibleLayout.

sections.title: Entrance easing
sections.summary: Shapes how the entrance speeds up and slows down. The default, Ease Out, starts quickly and settles gently; Ease Out Back adds a slight overshoot, and Linear moves at a constant speed. It sits under Advanced and only appears while Screen Entrance is on, and most screens can keep the default.

sections.title: Entrance duration
sections.summary: How long each animated element's entrance lasts, in milliseconds, from 50 to 10,000; Screen Entrance starts at 450. Around 300 to 600 ms feels quick and polished, while long entrances make visitors wait before they can read and tap. The preview replays after every change, so you can judge the speed right away.

sections.title: Entrance style
sections.summary: Chooses how each animated element appears when the screen opens: fades, slides, scales, zooms, bounces, flips, and more, many with a choice of direction. Fade In Up is the default and suits almost any screen. Keep calm fades and slides on question and paywall screens, and save bouncy or flipping styles for a playful brand or a single highlight moment.

sections.title: Delay between elements
sections.summary: The pause, in milliseconds, before each next element starts its entrance, so the screen builds up in order instead of appearing all at once. Set it from 0 to 1,000: Screen Entrance starts at 80, and 0 makes all elements enter together. Elements you give their own entrance under Advanced, and answer choices with an Item Animation, start right away instead of waiting their turn. Keep it small, since the pauses add up for elements later in the order, such as the action bar.

sections.title: Give this screen its own entrance
sections.summary: Turns on this screen's own entrance: its standard elements, such as the header, images, title, and action bar, animate in one after another in a fixed order when a visitor arrives. Switching it on starts with Fade In Up, 450 ms, and an 80 ms stagger (adjust them below) and overrides your theme's entrance for this screen. Switched off, the screen plays the Legacy fade-in if that toggle is on, otherwise your theme's entrance (shown as 'Inherited from theme'), or no entrance if the theme has none.

sections.title: Legacy fade-in
sections.summary: Shows under Legacy on screens that had it switched on when you opened the editor and have no Screen Entrance set. That includes older screens, and screens whose entrance came from a theme's motion scheme once you switch Screen Entrance off. While on, the screen plays a simple fade-in as it appears; turn on Screen Entrance above to replace it with the style, speed, and stagger you choose. Switched off, the screen follows your theme's entrance, or appears without one if the theme has none.
